item.content:encoded:
The 2027 The Africa Institute Senior and Postdoctoral Fellowships offer an opportunity for established scholars, emerging researchers, authors, and public intellectuals to undertake advanced research in African and African diaspora studies. Hosted by The Africa Institute, Global Studies University, the fellowships provide a dedicated research environment in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates, with opportunities for scholars to develop research projects in the humanities, social sciences, literature, cultural studies, visual culture, performance studies, and related fields.

Deadline: September 30, 2026

The fellowship programme is particularly relevant to researchers whose work contributes to a deeper understanding of Africa, the African diaspora, culture, society, history, gender, feminism, literature, visual culture, and related areas of critical scholarship.

About The Africa Institute

The Africa Institute, Global Studies University is a globally oriented centre focused on research, documentation, study, and teaching related to Africa and its diaspora, particularly within the humanities and social sciences.

The Institute is designed both as a research-based think tank and a postgraduate studies institution. It offers master’s and Ph.D. programmes intended to help develop a new generation of scholars and critical thinkers working on African and African diaspora studies.

Through its Research Fellowships Program, the Institute hosts senior and postdoctoral scholars who are given the opportunity to pursue focused research while participating in an academic environment dedicated to African and diaspora scholarship.

The 2027 fellowship programme includes four distinct fellowship opportunities, divided between senior scholars and postdoctoral researchers.

The 2027 Fellowship Opportunities

1. Toni Morrison Senior Fellowship in African Diaspora Literature and Cultural Studies

The Toni Morrison Senior Fellowship in African Diaspora Literature and Cultural Studies honours the legacy of Toni Morrison and her significant contributions to world literature, humanities, cultural studies, critical theory, and understanding of the African American experience.

The fellowship is intended for established scholars and intellectuals whose work relates to African and African diaspora literature, culture, and related fields.

Who can apply?

Eligible applicants may include:

  • Associate Professors or Full Professors at their home institutions
  • Independent authors
  • Public intellectuals
  • Established writers and scholars with recognised contributions in relevant fields
  • Researchers whose work focuses on African and African diaspora literature, culture, humanities, or related areas

Applicants should have demonstrated recognition for their writing or scholarly contributions.

Fellowship duration and location

This is a:

  • Full-time fellowship
  • One-year residency
  • Based in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates
  • Typically running from September to June

The residency format provides fellows with an opportunity to dedicate substantial time to their proposed research project.

2. Ali A. Mazrui Senior Fellowship in Global African Studies

The Ali A. Mazrui Senior Fellowship in Global African Studies is named in honour of Professor Ali A. Mazrui, whose work made major contributions to African Studies and its development as a global field of scholarship.

This fellowship is designed for established scholars whose research focuses on Africa and the African diaspora, particularly where these subjects intersect with the humanities and social sciences.

Areas of relevance

Potential research areas may include work examining:

  • African studies
  • African diaspora studies
  • Social sciences
  • Humanities
  • African societies and cultures
  • Global African studies
  • Intersections between Africa and the wider world

Who can apply?

The fellowship is open to:

  • Associate Professors
  • Full Professors
  • Scholars at equivalent levels outside traditional academic institutions
  • Independent authors
  • Public intellectuals
  • Recognised scholars whose work relates to African and African diaspora studies

Applicants should have established scholarly or intellectual recognition in relevant areas.

Fellowship duration and location

The Ali A. Mazrui Senior Fellowship provides:

  • A full-time research residency
  • One-year duration
  • Residence in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates
  • A typical fellowship period from September to June

3. Okwui Enwezor Postdoctoral Fellowship in Visual Culture, Performance Studies, and Critical Humanities

The Okwui Enwezor Postdoctoral Fellowship is intended for emerging scholars working in areas connected to visual culture, performance studies, art history, art criticism, and critical humanities.

The fellowship honours Okwui Enwezor and his influential contributions as a scholar, curator, and art critic.

Applicants should have research interests that connect visual or performance studies with broader debates in the humanities and African and African diaspora studies.

Potential areas of research

Relevant work may involve:

  • Visual culture
  • Performance studies
  • Art history
  • Art criticism
  • Cultural studies
  • Critical humanities
  • African and African diaspora perspectives in visual and performance studies

Who can apply?

Applicants must:

  • Be emerging scholars
  • Hold a Ph.D.
  • Have earned their doctoral degree within the five years preceding the start of the fellowship
  • Have research relevant to the fellowship’s thematic areas

Fellowship duration and location

The fellowship is:

  • Full-time
  • Two years
  • Based in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates
  • Typically running from September to June

This longer residency allows postdoctoral researchers to dedicate significant time to developing and completing their research.

4. Fatema Mernissi Postdoctoral Fellowship in Social and Cultural Studies

The Fatema Mernissi Postdoctoral Fellowship in Social and Cultural Studies honours the work of Professor Fatema Mernissi, whose scholarship made important contributions to gender, feminism, sociopolitical change, Islam, and cultural studies.

The fellowship is intended for emerging scholars working in the social sciences, particularly researchers whose work focuses on gender, feminism, cultural studies, or visual cultures and intersects with African and African diaspora studies.

Relevant research areas

Research may relate to:

  • Gender studies
  • Feminism
  • Social sciences
  • Cultural studies
  • Visual cultures
  • Sociopolitical change
  • African studies
  • African diaspora studies
  • Intersections between these fields

Who can apply?

Applicants must:

  • Be emerging scholars
  • Hold a Ph.D.
  • Have received their Ph.D. within the five years preceding the start of the fellowship
  • Have research relevant to social and cultural studies
  • Demonstrate a connection between their proposed research and African or African diaspora studies

Fellowship duration and location

The fellowship provides:

  • A full-time research residency
  • Two-year duration
  • Residence in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates
  • A typical fellowship period from September to June

Eligibility Criteria for the 2027 Fellowships

The programme has different eligibility requirements depending on whether applicants are applying for a Senior Fellowship or a Postdoctoral Fellowship.

Senior Fellowships

The Senior Fellowships are open to scholars who are:

  • Associate Professors
  • Full Professors
  • At equivalent levels within or outside academia
  • Established authors or public intellectuals with recognised contributions in relevant fields

Applicants should have an established record of intellectual or scholarly work related to the fellowship’s research area.

Postdoctoral Fellowships

Applicants for the Postdoctoral Fellowships must:

  • Hold a Ph.D.
  • Have received the Ph.D. within the last five years before assuming the fellowship
  • Have a research project relevant to the specific fellowship
  • Be emerging scholars working in the relevant academic or research field

Because each fellowship has its own thematic focus, applicants should select the fellowship that most closely matches their research interests and proposed project.

Application Requirements

Applicants are expected to prepare a research-focused application demonstrating the significance, objectives, and approach of their proposed work.

The application requires the following materials:

1. Research Abstract

Applicants must submit an abstract of up to 300 words.

The abstract should outline:

  • The proposed research project
  • The central focus of the research
  • What the applicant intends to investigate during the fellowship period

The abstract should provide a clear overview of the proposed project.

2. Project Statement

Applicants must submit a 1,000–2,000-word project statement explaining their proposed research.

The statement should address:

  • Research objectives
  • Research approach
  • Overall importance of the study
  • The central research questions or issues
  • The significance of the proposed work

Applicants may also include a one-page bibliography containing the key sources relevant to their proposed research.

3. Two Writing Samples

Applicants must provide two samples of writing.

The samples may be:

  • Published works
  • Unpublished works

These samples allow the Institute to assess the applicant’s research and writing ability.

4. Letter of Interest

Applicants must provide a letter of interest explaining their interest in the fellowship and their proposed research.

5. Curriculum Vitae

A current CV should be included with the application, presenting the applicant’s academic, research, professional, and publication background.

6. Referees

Applicants must provide the contact details of three referees.

The Institute will contact the referees directly to request letters of reference.

Applicants should therefore ensure that the contact information provided is accurate and that their referees are appropriate individuals who can comment meaningfully on their academic or professional work.

How to Choose the Right Fellowship

Applicants should carefully match their academic background and proposed research to the fellowship’s thematic focus.

Choose the Toni Morrison Senior Fellowship if:

Your work focuses on African diaspora literature, literature, culture, humanities, cultural studies, or critical theory, and you are an established scholar, author, or public intellectual.

Choose the Ali A. Mazrui Senior Fellowship if:

You are an established scholar working broadly in African and African diaspora studies, particularly across the humanities and social sciences.

Choose the Okwui Enwezor Postdoctoral Fellowship if:

You recently completed your Ph.D. and your research focuses on visual culture, performance studies, art history, art criticism, or critical humanities.

Choose the Fatema Mernissi Postdoctoral Fellowship if:

You recently completed your Ph.D. and your research focuses on gender, feminism, social sciences, cultural studies, visual cultures, and their relationship to Africa or the African diaspora.

Fellowship Location

All four fellowships are based in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates.

The fellowships are structured as residency programmes, meaning successful fellows are expected to undertake their research on a full-time basis at the Institute.

The senior fellowships are generally one-year residencies, while the postdoctoral fellowships are generally two-year residencies.

The typical fellowship period runs from September to June.

Why This Fellowship Opportunity Is Significant

The Africa Institute’s fellowship programme is particularly relevant to researchers seeking a dedicated environment for advanced work on Africa and the African diaspora.

The programme brings together different areas of scholarship, including:

  • African and African diaspora studies
  • Humanities
  • Social sciences
  • Literature
  • Cultural studies
  • Gender and feminism
  • Visual culture
  • Performance studies
  • Art history
  • Critical humanities

For established scholars, the Senior Fellowships provide an opportunity to pursue focused research at an advanced stage of their careers.

For recently graduated Ph.D. researchers, the Postdoctoral Fellowships provide an opportunity to develop their research within an institution specifically dedicated to African and African diaspora studies.

Important Deadline

The application deadline for the 2027 The Africa Institute Senior and Postdoctoral Fellowships is:

September 30, 2026

Applicants should prepare their research proposal, writing samples, CV, letter of interest, and referee information well before the deadline.

How to Apply

Applicants should prepare all required application materials and submit their application through the official fellowship application process.

Click HERE to read more and apply.

Conclusion

The 2027 The Africa Institute Senior and Postdoctoral Fellowships provide a research opportunity for established scholars and emerging postdoctoral researchers whose work contributes to the study of Africa and the African diaspora.

With four specialised fellowships covering African diaspora literature and cultural studies, global African studies, visual culture and performance studies, and social and cultural studies, the programme offers different pathways for researchers with diverse academic interests.

The fellowships are based in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates, and provide full-time research residencies ranging from one to two years depending on the fellowship.

Researchers interested in applying should ensure that their proposed project clearly aligns with the relevant fellowship, prepare a strong research statement and writing samples, and submit their application before the September 30, 2026 deadline.

Click HERE for more fellowship opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
The World Trade Organization (WTO) has opened nominations for the second edition of the WTO Youth Talent Incubator Programme, a global initiative designed to support the next generation of researchers and professionals working at the intersection of international trade, gender equality and women’s economic empowerment.

Running from 12 October 2026 to 30 June 2027, the programme offers young talent an opportunity to strengthen their expertise through mentoring, capacity building, applied learning and international networking. Participants will have opportunities to engage with global experts, WTO Members and other stakeholders working on trade and gender issues.

The programme is particularly relevant for young researchers whose academic or professional work already addresses trade and gender, as well as those seeking to incorporate these issues into their current research or policy work.

About the WTO Youth Talent Incubator Programme

The Youth Talent Incubator Programme was developed from the momentum generated by the World Trade Congress on Gender, which was first held at the WTO in December 2022. The Congress brought together leading experts working on trade and gender research and created opportunities for researchers and policymakers to exchange knowledge and establish partnerships.

The initiative subsequently contributed to the Youth Trade Summit on Gender, held in November 2023, which brought together 50 young professionals from academic institutions, research centres, think tanks and government authorities from around the world.

The Summit gave young researchers and early-career professionals opportunities to interact with WTO member delegations, senior researchers and international stakeholders on topics including women’s economic empowerment and the relationship between gender and international trade.

The first Youth Talent Incubator Programme was launched in July 2024. Over an eleven-month period, participants developed their knowledge and professional skills through mentorship, applied policy research, training and networking. The outcomes of that programme were presented to the WTO Informal Working Group on Trade and Gender in December 2025.

Building on these achievements, the second edition will run from 12 October 2026 to 30 June 2027.

What the Programme Focuses On

The WTO Youth Talent Incubator Programme is built around three main pillars:

1. Mentoring

Participants will benefit from engagement with experienced researchers, experts and professionals in the trade and gender field.

Mentoring is intended to help young participants develop their ideas, strengthen their professional direction and deepen their understanding of how trade and gender issues are addressed in research and policymaking.

2. Capacity Building

The programme provides opportunities for participants to strengthen their technical knowledge and professional skills related to trade and gender.

This is particularly valuable for young researchers and professionals who want to connect academic research with practical policy challenges and evidence-based solutions.

3. Networking

Participants will have opportunities to build connections with global experts, WTO Members and other international and regional stakeholders.

The networking component can help participants expand their professional networks and become more connected to the global trade and gender community.

Why Trade and Gender Matter

The programme comes at a time when governments, international organisations and other public and private stakeholders increasingly recognise the relationship between women’s economic empowerment, international trade and sustainable development.

Improving women’s participation in international trade requires not only policy action but also strong research and evidence. Researchers play an important role by examining existing challenges, identifying inequalities and developing evidence-based approaches that policymakers can use.

The WTO has progressively integrated gender considerations into its work since 2017 through political commitments, technical policy work, research, capacity building and practical trade-policy tools.

In 2020, the WTO Informal Working Group on Trade and Gender was established. According to the call, the group now represents more than 80% of WTO membership and has become the main platform within the WTO for discussions on trade and gender.

The WTO’s work in this area has continued to develop through successive Ministerial Conferences. At the 14th WTO Ministerial Conference in March 2026, the Informal Working Group achieved several member-led outcomes, including:

  • A joint statement on strengthening the global trading system through women’s economic empowerment.
  • An achievements tracking compendium documenting gender-responsive trade initiatives since 2020.
  • A new initiative, developed with the Informal Working Group on MSMEs, to create a compendium on empowering women to trade through digitalisation.
  • Additional practical policy tools to support women’s economic empowerment through trade.

These developments demonstrate the growing importance of researchers and young professionals who can contribute evidence, ideas and policy recommendations to the global trade and gender conversation.

Who Is the WTO Seeking to Nominate?

The WTO Gender Research Hub is seeking nominations for young researchers and young professionals working in relevant academic, research and government environments.

Potential nominees may come from:

  • Universities and academic institutions
  • Research foundations
  • Research centres
  • Think tanks
  • Policy research organisations
  • Government institutions
  • Other relevant research and policy settings

The programme is designed for young researchers in academia and research institutions, as well as young professionals working in government.

Learn more HERE

Eligibility and Nomination Criteria

Candidates must satisfy the programme’s nomination requirements.

Age

Applicants must generally be 20 to 35 years old.

The call also notes that the age limit may be relaxed in exceptional circumstances. This may apply to nominees who demonstrate outstanding initiative or who have taken a career break. Candidates seeking such an exception should explain their circumstances in their motivation letter.

Interest or Current Work in Trade and Gender

Candidates must demonstrate current work relating to trade and gender, or show a clear interest in incorporating trade and gender issues into their existing work.

This means applicants should be able to demonstrate a genuine connection to the subject rather than simply expressing a general interest in international development.

Motivation Letter

Candidates must provide a motivation letter explaining their interest and suitability for the programme.

A strong motivation letter should clearly communicate the candidate’s existing work, professional or research interests and reasons for wanting to engage more deeply with trade and gender issues.

Institutional Endorsement

Candidates must be formally endorsed by their academic or research institution.

The call specifically refers to institutions such as think tanks, research foundations and centres and policy research settings.

This is important because the programme is not structured as an entirely individual application. The candidate must be nominated and endorsed through an eligible academic or research institution.

How the Selection Process Works

The call for nominations is directed to academic and research institutions.

Nominations may be submitted by legal representatives of eligible institutions through the designated online nomination form.

Up to 35 nominees will ultimately be selected by the Chair of the WTO Gender Research Hub to participate in the second edition of the Youth Talent Incubator Programme.

Selected applicants are scheduled to receive notification of the outcome by email on 1 October 2026.

Programme Format and Cost

The programme will be conducted entirely online, making it accessible to selected participants without requiring relocation to Geneva or another physical programme location.

Importantly, the programme is cost-free for participants.

This online format can be particularly valuable for young researchers and professionals who are working or studying while participating in the programme.

Programme Dates

The second edition of the WTO Youth Talent Incubator Programme will run from:

12 October 2026 to 30 June 2027.

The selected participants will therefore have an extended period to engage with mentoring, capacity-building and networking activities.

Application Deadline

The deadline for nominations is 24 September 2026 at 23:59 CET.

The WTO states explicitly that the deadline will not be extended, so eligible institutions and potential nominees should begin the nomination process well in advance.

Important Point About the Application Process

Potential candidates should note that the call is specifically seeking nominations from academic and research institutions.

Therefore, an eligible young researcher or professional should not assume that simply submitting an individual application will satisfy the requirements. Candidates should work with their university, research centre, think tank, foundation or relevant institution to secure the required formal endorsement.

Institutions should ensure that the nomination is submitted through the appropriate online form before the deadline.

Contact Information

For questions concerning the Youth Talent Incubator Programme or the nomination process, applicants and institutions can contact the WTO’s Trade and Gender Office at:

trade-gender@wto.org

Additional information about the programme is available through the WTO website.

How to Prepare a Strong Nomination

Although meeting the eligibility criteria is essential, candidates can strengthen their prospects by preparing a clear and convincing nomination.

Consider the following:

  1. Clearly demonstrate your connection to trade and gender. Explain your current research, professional work or academic interests and how they relate to these themes.
  2. Show evidence of commitment. Where possible, highlight research projects, publications, policy work, academic activities or professional experiences related to gender, trade, women’s economic empowerment or related policy issues.
  3. Write a focused motivation letter. Explain why participation in the Youth Talent Incubator Programme is important for your research or career development.
  4. Approach your institution early. Because institutional endorsement is required, do not wait until the final day to begin discussions with your university, research centre, think tank or other eligible institution.
  5. Demonstrate future potential. Explain how the knowledge, mentoring and networks gained through the programme could contribute to your future research, professional work or policy engagement.
  6. Connect your work to broader policy challenges. Strong candidates should be able to demonstrate an understanding of why gender-responsive trade policies matter for sustainable development and women’s economic empowerment.

APPLY HERE

Why This Opportunity Is Valuable

The WTO Youth Talent Incubator Programme provides a distinctive opportunity for emerging researchers and professionals to develop within an international policy environment.

Participants can potentially gain:

  • Exposure to international trade and gender policy discussions.
  • Mentorship from experienced experts.
  • Capacity-building opportunities.
  • Greater understanding of the relationship between trade and gender.
  • Opportunities to engage with WTO Members and international stakeholders.
  • International professional networking.
  • Experience connecting research with policy.
  • A platform for contributing young people’s perspectives to global discussions.
  • Participation in a global community focused on advancing gender-responsive trade policy.

The programme can therefore be particularly relevant to individuals considering careers in international organisations, public policy, trade policy, gender equality, economic development, research, academia and international relations.

Visit HERE to learn more about the WTO Youth Talent Incubator Programme.

Conclusion

The WTO Youth Talent Incubator Programme – 2nd Edition represents an important opportunity for young researchers and professionals seeking to deepen their engagement with the relationship between international trade and gender equality.

With its three pillars of mentoring, capacity building and networking, the programme is designed to help develop the next generation of trade and gender experts while strengthening connections between research and policymaking. The entirely online and cost-free format further makes the programme accessible to selected participants from different professional and academic environments.

Young researchers and professionals who meet the criteria should begin working with their eligible academic or research institutions as soon as possible, particularly because institutional endorsement is required and the nomination deadline is 24 September 2026 at 23:59 CET.

Discover more global Fellowship and Research opportunities on OFY.

item.content:encoded:
The Microsoft Account Technology Strategist (ATS) – BBBEE Internship is an opportunity for recent graduates and eligible final-year students in South Africa to gain practical experience in technology strategy, customer engagement, digital transformation, cloud computing, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and modern workplace solutions.

The internship is offered by Microsoft South Africa and is designed to help talented young professionals build technical, business, communication, and customer-facing skills while working on real-world projects.

Microsoft Account Technology Strategist BBBEE Internship 2026

As an Account Technology Strategist Intern, you will work with Microsoft account teams and customers to understand business and technology challenges and help identify solutions that can support digital transformation.

The role combines technology, business strategy, sales, customer engagement, and digital transformation, making it particularly relevant for graduates who want to build careers in technology consulting, technology sales, account management, business development, cloud solutions, or digital transformation.

The position is based in:

  • Johannesburg, Gauteng, South Africa
  • Work arrangement: Fully on-site
  • Travel: Less than 25%
  • Profession: Technology Sales
  • Discipline: Account Technology
  • Role type: Individual Contributor
  • Employment type: Internship
  • Job number: 200049855
  • Date posted: 31 August 2026

About the Microsoft South Africa BBBEE Internship Programme

The Microsoft South Africa BBBEE Internship Programme provides eligible graduates with an opportunity to gain hands-on professional experience while developing technical and workplace skills.

Interns have the opportunity to:

  • Work on meaningful projects.
  • Receive professional mentorship.
  • Develop technical and business skills.
  • Collaborate with Microsoft teams.
  • Work with customers and business decision-makers.
  • Gain exposure to emerging technologies.
  • Develop a foundation for future career opportunities.

The programme also supports Microsoft’s broader commitment to skills development, transformation, and inclusive economic growth in South Africa.

What Does an Account Technology Strategist Intern Do?

The Account Technology Strategist role focuses on helping customers understand how technology can address their business challenges.

As an intern, you will support Microsoft account teams and participate in activities such as:

1. Understanding customer needs

You will work with account teams to understand customers’ business priorities, technology challenges, and digital transformation goals.

This involves learning how organizations operate and identifying areas where technology could improve their performance.

2. Supporting technology discussions

Interns will assist with technology discussions involving customers and help communicate how Microsoft solutions can create business value.

This provides practical exposure to customer engagement and technology sales.

3. Researching industries and market trends

The role involves researching:

  • Customer industries
  • Market trends
  • Technology developments
  • Digital transformation opportunities
  • Business challenges
  • Emerging technology solutions

This research can help account teams identify opportunities for innovation and growth.

4. Developing technology roadmaps

Interns may assist in preparing customer technology roadmaps, presentations, and solution recommendations.

This provides experience in translating customer needs into practical technology strategies.

5. Working with cross-functional teams

The intern will collaborate with different Microsoft teams, including:

  • Sales teams
  • Solution architects
  • Technical specialists
  • Customer success teams
  • Account teams

This gives interns exposure to how large technology organizations coordinate different functions to serve customers.

6. Supporting account planning

Interns will contribute to account planning activities and help identify opportunities for customer growth, innovation, and digital transformation.

7. Learning Microsoft technologies

The internship provides exposure to major technology areas, including:

  • Microsoft Azure
  • Artificial intelligence
  • Cybersecurity
  • Modern Work
  • Business Applications
  • Cloud transformation

Who Can Apply?

This internship has specific eligibility requirements.

Applicants must be:

  • South African citizens who meet the eligibility requirements of the Microsoft South Africa BBBEE Internship Programme.
  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in an eligible field and be in their final year with no more than six months remaining, or
  • Have completed a Bachelor’s degree within the last six months.

Relevant fields of study include:

  • Computer Science
  • Information Technology
  • Engineering
  • Data Science
  • Business Information Systems
  • Related fields

Applicants should also demonstrate:

  • Fluency in English.
  • Strong analytical skills.
  • Strong problem-solving abilities.
  • Good communication skills.
  • Interest in technology and innovation.
  • Interest in customer engagement.
  • Ability to explain technical concepts to technical and non-technical audiences.

Click HERE to read more.

Benefits of the Internship

The Microsoft Account Technology Strategist BBBEE Internship can provide valuable early-career experience in one of the world’s leading technology companies.

Key benefits include:

Practical experience

Interns can gain hands-on experience working on real-world technology and customer projects.

Professional development

The programme is designed to help participants develop both technical and professional skills.

Mentorship and collaboration

Interns have opportunities to learn from experienced professionals and collaborate with teams across Microsoft.

Exposure to emerging technology

Participants can gain exposure to areas such as Azure, AI, cybersecurity, Business Applications, and Modern Work.

Customer-facing experience

The ATS role provides experience communicating with business and technology decision-makers and understanding customer needs.

Career foundation

The experience can help graduates build a foundation for careers in technology sales, account technology, consulting, digital transformation, business development, and related areas.

Important Application Information

The position was posted on 31 August 2026.

Unlike opportunities with a fixed closing date, Microsoft states that applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled.

Therefore, applicants should not wait for a specific final deadline. The position is stated to be open for a minimum of five days, with applications reviewed while the position remains available.

Application status: Open

How to Apply

Interested candidates should carefully review the eligibility requirements and submit their application through Microsoft’s official careers platform.

APPLY HERE

Applicants should ensure that their CV clearly demonstrates their relevant academic background, technical skills, analytical abilities, communication skills, and interest in technology and customer engagement.

Important Eligibility Note

This is not an international internship open to applicants from every country.

The programme specifically states that applicants must be South African citizens and satisfy the eligibility requirements of the Microsoft South Africa BBBEE Internship Programme.

Therefore, candidates from other African countries, including Ethiopia, should not assume that they are eligible simply because the position is located in Africa. The stated citizenship requirement is specifically South African citizenship.

Conclusion

The Microsoft Account Technology Strategist BBBEE Internship 2026 offers eligible South African students and recent graduates an opportunity to gain practical experience at the intersection of technology, business strategy, customer engagement, and digital transformation.

With exposure to technologies such as Azure, AI, cybersecurity, Modern Work, and Business Applications, the internship can be particularly valuable for candidates interested in building careers in technology sales, consulting, account management, digital transformation, or business development.

Because Microsoft states that applications are accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled, eligible candidates should consider applying as early as possible rather than waiting for a closing date.

Click HERE for more internship opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
The International Olympic Committee (IOC) Olympic Studies Centre (OSC) has officially launched the 2027 PhD Students and Early Career Academics Research Grant Programme, providing an important research opportunity for emerging scholars whose academic work focuses on Olympism, the Olympic Movement, the Olympic Games, athletes, and the broader social and cultural impact of sport.

The programme is designed to support researchers at an early stage of their academic careers by providing funding that can contribute to the development and completion of scholarly research. It can also provide eligible researchers with an opportunity to access the extensive academic and historical resources held by the IOC Olympic Studies Centre in Lausanne, Switzerland.

Since the programme was established in 1999, more than 148 researchers from around the world have benefited from the initiative, receiving grants that have supported their research activities and, where appropriate, enabled them to visit the Olympic Studies Centre and consult its specialised collections.

For researchers working in the humanities and social sciences, particularly those examining the Olympic Games and their relationship with contemporary society, this programme represents a significant opportunity to advance academic research while gaining access to one of the world’s major collections of Olympic-related knowledge.

Opportunity Overview

The 2027 PhD Students and Early Career Academics Research Grant Programme is intended for postgraduate researchers and early-career academics undertaking research related to the Olympic world.

The programme focuses on scholarly research concerning areas such as:

  • Olympism and its ideals
  • The Olympic Movement
  • The Olympic Games
  • Olympic history
  • Athletes and their experiences
  • Sport and contemporary society
  • Sport and culture
  • The social impact of the Olympic Games
  • The cultural significance of Olympism
  • Historical, political, economic or social dimensions of the Olympic Movement
  • Other relevant topics within the human and social sciences that incorporate Olympism, the Olympic Movement or the Olympic Games as a research focus

The programme therefore goes beyond research that examines sporting competitions themselves. It can be relevant to academic projects exploring how the Olympic Movement interacts with wider questions concerning society, culture, history and contemporary life.

What Is the IOC Olympic Studies Centre?

The IOC Olympic Studies Centre is an important research and knowledge centre dedicated to Olympic studies. It provides researchers with access to specialised collections, academic publications, historical materials and other resources relating to the Olympic Movement.

Researchers interested in learning more about the centre and its activities can visit the IOC Olympic Studies Centre official website.

The centre’s resources can be particularly valuable for scholars who require historical documents, academic literature, official Olympic publications and archival material to strengthen their research.

Who Can Apply for the 2027 Research Grant Programme?

The programme is specifically targeted at current PhD students and early-career academics.

There are two principal categories of eligible applicants.

1. Current PhD Students

Current postgraduate students may apply if they are enrolled in a PhD degree programme within the human and/or social sciences and their research incorporates at least one of the following as a research focus:

  • Olympism
  • The Olympic Movement
  • The Olympic Games

This means that applicants do not necessarily need to be studying a programme titled “Olympic Studies.” Instead, their research should have a meaningful connection to one or more of these areas.

For example, a PhD project could potentially examine the social impact of the Olympic Games, the historical development of the Olympic Movement, the relationship between Olympism and society, the cultural significance of major sporting events, or another appropriate topic within the human and social sciences.

2. Early-Career Academics and Postdoctoral Fellows

Academic staff members and postdoctoral fellows can also be eligible.

To qualify under this category, applicants must have completed their doctorate or equivalent highest degree in or after 2024.

The eligibility provisions also recognise that the highest relevant qualification may vary depending on the academic field. In some fields, this may include a master’s degree as the equivalent highest degree.

This makes the programme particularly relevant to researchers who have recently completed their advanced academic qualifications and are beginning to establish their independent research careers.

What Can the Grant Support?

One of the most valuable aspects of the programme is its connection with the IOC Olympic Studies Centre’s research infrastructure.

Researchers who receive support can use the opportunity to advance their scholarly work and, where relevant, visit the Olympic Studies Centre in Lausanne, Switzerland to consult its collections.

This can be particularly useful for projects requiring access to primary sources, historical documentation and specialised Olympic literature.

The programme has therefore provided more than simply financial assistance to researchers. Its connection to the Olympic Studies Centre can also help scholars engage with resources that may be highly relevant to their research questions.

Access to the Olympic World Library

Researchers interested in Olympic studies can also explore the Olympic World Library (OWL), the IOC’s specialised library catalogue dedicated to Olympic knowledge.

The collection contains more than 42,000 official and academic publications, making it a valuable starting point for researchers looking for literature and documentation related to Olympic studies.

The Olympic World Library can help researchers identify relevant academic and official publications when developing their literature reviews, theoretical frameworks and research background.

The availability of such a specialised collection can be particularly valuable for PhD researchers who need to demonstrate a strong understanding of existing scholarship and historical developments within their research areas.

IOC Historical Archives

In addition to the library resources, researchers can access information about the IOC’s historical archives through the Olympic Studies Centre.

The historical archives can provide important material for scholars examining the development of the Olympic Movement, institutional history, Olympic events and other historical dimensions of Olympism.

Researchers can explore the IOC Historical Archives for further information.

For researchers undertaking historical or documentary research, these resources may provide valuable primary and contextual material that can complement conventional academic sources.

Grant Programme Selection Committee

Applications are assessed by a Grant Programme Selection Committee composed of academic experts internationally recognised for their involvement in Olympic studies, together with representatives of the Olympic Studies Centre.

The composition of the committee highlights the academic nature of the programme and the importance of the quality and relevance of applicants’ proposed research.

Applicants should therefore approach the application as a serious academic research proposal rather than simply submitting a general expression of interest.

A strong application should clearly demonstrate the academic value of the research, its relationship to Olympic studies and why the proposed research requires the support and resources associated with the programme.

How Applicants Can Strengthen Their Applications

Although applicants should follow the official programme rules and guidelines carefully, prospective candidates should pay particular attention to the connection between their research and the programme’s objectives.

1. Clearly establish the Olympic connection

The research should have a clear and meaningful relationship with Olympism, the Olympic Movement or the Olympic Games.

Applicants should avoid relying on a superficial reference to sport or the Olympics. The Olympic dimension should form a genuine part of the research focus.

2. Present a clear research question

A well-defined research question can help demonstrate the academic significance of the proposed project.

Applicants should be able to explain:

  • What they are researching
  • Why the subject matters
  • What knowledge gap the research addresses
  • How the research will contribute to existing scholarship
  • What methods they intend to use
  • What sources or materials are required

3. Demonstrate academic relevance

Applicants should clearly position their proposed project within the relevant human or social sciences discipline.

This could involve explaining how the research contributes to existing discussions in fields such as history, sociology, cultural studies, political studies, economics, communication, education or another relevant discipline.

4. Make effective use of available research resources

Where appropriate, applicants should explain how the collections and resources of the Olympic Studies Centre could contribute to their research.

If a project would benefit from consulting primary sources, historical archives or specialised Olympic publications, this should be articulated clearly in the application.

5. Follow the application instructions carefully

Applicants should consult the official rules and guidelines before preparing their submission. The programme’s requirements, documentation and submission procedures should be followed precisely.

The official IOC Olympic Studies Centre page provides the central source for programme information.

Application Rules and Guidelines

The programme has published official rules and guidelines to assist prospective applicants.

Researchers should read these documents carefully before completing their application. The guidelines are particularly important because they provide the formal requirements governing the programme and the application process.

The official programme documentation should be treated as the authoritative source when determining eligibility, preparing application materials and submitting correspondence.

Application Form

Eligible researchers are required to complete the relevant application documentation provided for the programme.

Applicants should ensure that all requested information is supplied accurately and that their research proposal is presented clearly and professionally.

Before submission, candidates should check their application against the official requirements to ensure that no required component has been overlooked.

Application Deadline

The deadline for applications to the 2027 PhD Students and Early Career Academics Research Grant Programme is Tuesday, 22 September 2026.

All application files and related correspondence should be sent to the Olympic Studies Centre before the deadline.

Deadline: 22 September 2026

Researchers should avoid waiting until the final day to submit their applications. Preparing a competitive academic application can require considerable time, particularly where a research proposal, supporting documents or institutional information must be reviewed before submission.

Online Information Sessions

The Olympic Studies Centre is also offering two online information sessions for researchers intending to apply.

These sessions can be particularly useful for prospective applicants who want to better understand the programme and clarify aspects of the application process.

Researchers considering an application should consult the official programme rules and guidelines for information about these sessions and how they can participate.

Who Qualifies for This Opportunity?

The main qualifying groups are

  1. Current postgraduate students enrolled in a PhD programme within the human and/or social sciences.
  2. PhD students whose research incorporates Olympism, the Olympic Movement or the Olympic Games as at least one of their research focuses.
  3. Academic staff members who have completed their doctorate or equivalent highest degree in or after 2024.
  4. Postdoctoral fellows who completed their doctorate or equivalent highest degree in or after 2024.
  5. Applicants whose relevant highest qualification may be a master’s degree where the programme recognises a master’s as the equivalent highest degree for the relevant field.

Countries and Continents: Who Can Apply?

The programme is described as having benefited researchers from all over the world, and the information provided does not specify a restriction to particular countries or continents.

Therefore, the opportunity is international in scope, rather than being presented as a programme limited to a specific geographic region.

Researchers from Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Oceania and other parts of the world can therefore consider applying, provided they satisfy the academic eligibility requirements.

For applicants in Africa, including researchers from Kenya and other African countries, the key consideration is not geographical location but whether the applicant meets the programme’s academic and research requirements.

However, prospective applicants should always check the official programme rules for the definitive eligibility requirements before submitting an application.

Race or Ethnicity Requirements

The information provided for the programme does not identify race or ethnicity as an eligibility restriction.

The eligibility criteria are primarily based on the applicant’s academic status, qualifications and research focus.

Consequently, applicants should focus on demonstrating that they meet the programme’s academic requirements rather than assuming that the programme is restricted to a particular racial or ethnic group.

Academic Fields Relevant to the Programme

Because the programme targets research in the human and social sciences, it may be relevant to scholars working across a variety of disciplines, provided that their research has an appropriate connection to Olympism, the Olympic Movement or the Olympic Games.

Potentially relevant areas may include:

  • History
  • Sociology
  • Political science
  • International relations
  • Cultural studies
  • Anthropology
  • Economics
  • Communication and media studies
  • Education
  • Sports studies
  • Olympic studies
  • Social sciences
  • Humanities
  • Other related human and social science disciplines

The decisive factor is not simply the name of the academic discipline but the relationship between the proposed research and the programme’s focus.

Another Research Grant Programme for Established Researchers

The IOC Olympic Studies Centre also offers another research opportunity for more established academics: the Advanced Olympic Research Grant Programme.

This programme is aimed at university professors, lecturers and research fellows who have completed their doctorate and hold an academic or research appointment.

Unlike the PhD Students and Early Career Academics Research Grant Programme, the Advanced Olympic Research Grant Programme is intended to promote advanced research by established researchers in the humanities and social sciences.

Its priority research fields are identified by the IOC every two years.

The call for applications for the 2027–2029 edition of the Advanced Olympic Research Grant Programme is expected to be issued in October 2026.

Researchers who are already established in academic or research positions may therefore wish to monitor the IOC Olympic Studies Centre research grant programmes page for further information.

Why This Research Grant Matters for Emerging Scholars

Research funding can be particularly important for PhD students and early-career academics because developing high-quality scholarly research often requires access to specialised literature, primary sources, archives, travel and other research resources.

The IOC Olympic Studies Centre programme offers an opportunity that combines research support with access to an internationally recognised Olympic knowledge centre.

For eligible scholars, the programme can therefore contribute to several aspects of academic development, including

  • Advancing an existing PhD research project
  • Supporting scholarly investigation into Olympic-related topics
  • Accessing specialised Olympic publications
  • Consulting historical and primary-source material
  • Strengthening research based on archival evidence
  • Developing deeper expertise in Olympic studies
  • Connecting academic research with the history and ideals of the Olympic Movement
  • Expanding the evidence base for academic publications and research outputs

The programme’s history of supporting more than 148 researchers since 1999 also demonstrates its longstanding role in supporting academic research connected to Olympic studies.

How to Apply

Researchers interested in the programme should begin by reviewing the official information provided by the Olympic Studies Centre.

A sensible application process would involve the following steps:

Step 1: Confirm your eligibility

Determine whether you are currently enrolled in a qualifying PhD programme or whether you fall within the early-career academic or postdoctoral category.

Step 2: Assess your research topic

Confirm that Olympism, the Olympic Movement or the Olympic Games forms at least one of the central research focuses of your project.

Step 3: Review the official rules

Read the programme rules and guidelines carefully before preparing the application.

Step 4: Prepare your application

Complete the official application form and prepare all required supporting information.

Step 5: Consider the Olympic Studies Centre resources

Determine whether the Olympic World Library, IOC historical archives or other OSC collections could contribute to your research and explain the relevance where appropriate.

Step 6: Attend an information session

Where possible, take advantage of the online information sessions offered to prospective applicants.

Step 7: Submit before the deadline

Ensure that the complete application file and related correspondence reach the Olympic Studies Centre before 22 September 2026.

APPLY HERE

Official Application and Further Information

Researchers should use the official IOC Olympic Studies Centre resources when applying and should avoid relying solely on third-party summaries for eligibility or application requirements.

For programme information and access to the relevant application resources, visit the IOC Olympic Studies Centre.

Applicants can also explore the Olympic World Library and the IOC Historical Archives as part of their research preparation.

Visit HERE for more information about the IOC Olympic Studies Centre Research Grant Programme 2027.

Key Details at a Glance

Detail Information
Opportunity 2027 PhD Students and Early Career Academics Research Grant Programme
Organisation International Olympic Committee Olympic Studies Centre
Category Academic Research Grant
Target applicants PhD students, academic staff and postdoctoral fellows
Academic area Human and social sciences
Research focus Olympism, Olympic Movement and/or Olympic Games
Early-career requirement Doctorate or equivalent highest degree completed in or after 2024
Geographical scope International
Race/ethnicity restriction No specific restriction stated
Research resources Olympic World Library, IOC historical archives and OSC collections
Deadline 22 September 2026
Location of OSC Lausanne, Switzerland
Official information IOC Olympic Studies Centre

Conclusion

The IOC Olympic Studies Centre Research Grant Programme 2027 offers a valuable opportunity for PhD students and early-career academics seeking to advance research related to Olympism, the Olympic Movement and the Olympic Games.

Its combination of research support and access to specialised Olympic collections makes the programme particularly relevant to scholars in the humanities and social sciences who require high-quality academic, historical and primary-source material for their work.

The programme is international in scope and is aimed at researchers who meet the specified academic and research criteria, rather than being restricted to applicants from a particular country, continent, race or ethnicity.

With more than 148 researchers having benefited from the programme since its establishment in 1999, the initiative has a longstanding history of supporting scholarship in Olympic studies.

Eligible researchers should carefully review the official rules, prepare a strong and clearly focused research proposal, take advantage of the available information sessions and ensure that their complete application is submitted before the 22 September 2026 deadline.
