item.content:encoded:
Lancaster University is offering a wide range of exciting PhD and postgraduate research opportunities through its School of Mathematical Sciences. The fully funded PhD studentships provide an excellent opportunity for talented graduates and researchers interested in Mathematics, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and related quantitative disciplines to pursue advanced research at one of the United Kingdom’s leading mathematical sciences departments.

The School of Mathematical Sciences at Lancaster University supports doctoral researchers across diverse areas of Pure Mathematics, Statistics, Mathematical Artificial Intelligence, Probability, Applied Mathematics, Computational Mathematics and Social Statistics. Depending on the specific programme and funding route, successful candidates may receive support covering tuition fees, living expenses through a tax-free stipend, research training and opportunities to participate in international academic conferences.

With a strong research environment, internationally recognised academics and access to interdisciplinary research centres, Lancaster University provides an attractive destination for students seeking to build careers in academia, industry, data science, artificial intelligence, scientific computing and other research-intensive fields.

Study for a PhD at Lancaster University’s School of Mathematical Sciences

The School of Mathematical Sciences offers postgraduate research degrees across several specialised programmes. Students can pursue doctoral research in areas aligned with the expertise of Lancaster’s academic staff and research groups.

The available PhD programmes include:

  • PhD in Applied Mathematics
  • PhD in Mathematics
  • PhD in Mathematical AI
  • PhD in Statistics
  • Integrated PhD in Statistics
  • PhD in Social Statistics

The School is also connected to several major doctoral training and research initiatives, including the Statistics and Operational Research Centre for Doctoral Training (STOR-i), the North West Social Science Doctoral Training Partnership and the Exascale Computing for Earth, Environmental and Sustainability Solutions Doctoral Landscape Award.

These opportunities allow doctoral researchers to engage with advanced research questions while benefiting from interdisciplinary collaboration and professional development.

The conventional entry point for most PhD programmes is October at the beginning of the academic year. However, January and April entry may also be possible in certain circumstances.

Prospective applicants are encouraged to begin preparing their applications well in advance. Lancaster University recommends applying approximately six to twelve months before the intended start date, particularly for candidates seeking competitive funding opportunities.

Why Study Mathematical Sciences at Lancaster University?

Lancaster University’s School of Mathematical Sciences has developed a strong reputation for research excellence and impact.

The School achieved an impressive position in the Research Excellence Framework 2021, including recognition for the impact of its research. Its academics regularly contribute to internationally recognised research journals and secure funding from competitive research organisations.

Doctoral students benefit from an environment where mathematical theory is connected to practical challenges across science, technology, health, engineering and industry.

Key strengths of the School include:

  • Strong research performance in mathematical sciences
  • Internationally recognised academic staff
  • Opportunities for interdisciplinary research
  • Research connections with industry and external partners
  • Access to specialist doctoral training programmes
  • Support for independent research development
  • Opportunities to collaborate with researchers across different disciplines
  • Training for careers in academia and industry
  • Research activities covering Pure Mathematics, Statistics and Artificial Intelligence

The School reports that its research spans internationally excellent and world-leading areas, making it an attractive environment for ambitious postgraduate researchers.

Research Areas Available for PhD Students

One of the major advantages of applying to Lancaster University’s Mathematical Sciences PhD programmes is the broad range of research areas available.

Applicants are encouraged to explore the research interests of academic staff and identify supervisors whose expertise aligns with their academic background and future research interests.

Pure Mathematics

Students interested in theoretical and abstract mathematics may pursue research projects across several specialised areas.

Potential areas include:

  • Functional analysis
  • Operator algebras
  • Algebraic number theory
  • Representation theory
  • Algebraic geometry
  • Homological algebra
  • Noncommutative geometry
  • Quantum groups
  • Cluster algebras
  • Graph theory
  • Combinatorics
  • Discrete geometry
  • Analytic number theory
  • Additive combinatorics
  • Dynamical systems
  • Topological dynamics
  • Mathematical physics
  • Random matrices

Research in Pure Mathematics provides opportunities for students to investigate fundamental mathematical questions while developing advanced theoretical and analytical skills.

Statistics and Data Science

Lancaster University also offers extensive research opportunities in Statistics and related disciplines.

Potential areas of research include:

  • Bayesian inference
  • Machine learning
  • Probabilistic modelling
  • Time series analysis
  • Spatio-temporal modelling
  • Environmental statistics
  • Medical statistics
  • Epidemiological modelling
  • Statistical ecology
  • Extreme value theory
  • Changepoint detection
  • Anomaly detection
  • Computational statistics
  • High-dimensional statistics
  • Non-parametric statistics
  • Statistical genomics
  • Point processes
  • Cluster analysis
  • Unsupervised learning
  • Functional time series
  • Health data analysis

These research areas allow students to apply advanced statistical methods to real-world problems in healthcare, climate science, biology, environmental science, artificial intelligence and other sectors.

Applied Mathematics

Applicants with strong mathematical and computational backgrounds may also pursue doctoral research in Applied Mathematics.

Potential research areas include:

  • Mathematical modelling
  • Numerical analysis
  • Dynamical systems
  • Mathematical biology
  • Computational modelling
  • Materials modelling
  • Differential equations
  • Mathematical physics
  • Optimisation
  • Scientific computing
  • Biological network modelling
  • Engineering applications
  • Robotics and control systems

Applied Mathematics research can provide opportunities to work on complex scientific and technological problems requiring mathematical modelling and computational approaches.

Mathematics for Artificial Intelligence

Lancaster University is increasingly active in research connecting Mathematics with Artificial Intelligence.

The Mathematics for AI in Real-world Systems initiative supports research at the intersection of mathematical sciences, computational methods and artificial intelligence.

Potential research themes include:

  • Mathematical Artificial Intelligence
  • Machine learning
  • Optimisation algorithms
  • Probabilistic machine learning
  • AI modelling
  • Numerical methods
  • Mathematical foundations of AI
  • Statistical learning
  • Computational algorithms
  • Data-driven modelling

These interdisciplinary areas are particularly relevant for students interested in contributing to the rapidly expanding fields of AI, machine learning and data science.

Fully Funded PhD Studentships at Lancaster University

Lancaster University’s School of Mathematical Sciences offers several funding opportunities for postgraduate researchers.

Funding may come from different sources, including:

  1. Research Council Studentships
  2. Departmental Studentships
  3. ESRC Studentship Competitions
  4. Industry-funded Studentships
  5. External Research Funding
  6. Specialist Doctoral Training Centres

The specific financial support available depends on the programme and studentship.

Research Council Studentships

Research Council funding may provide:

  • Full payment of tuition fees
  • A stipend for living expenses

International students may also be eligible for some UK Research and Innovation-funded studentships, although restrictions may apply to the proportion of awards allocated to international candidates.

Departmental Studentships

Departmental studentships normally provide:

  • Tuition fee support at the applicable funding level
  • A stipend to contribute towards living expenses

Some studentships may be open to applicants regardless of nationality. However, international students should carefully check whether they may need to cover any difference between UK-level tuition funding and international tuition fees.

Industry and External Funding

Some PhD projects receive funding from industry partners and other external organisations.

These opportunities may include:

  • Tuition fee support
  • Living stipends
  • Research funding
  • Industry engagement
  • Applied research experience

Applicants should carefully review the requirements of each individual project because funding arrangements can differ.

PhD Studentships in Pure Mathematics and Statistics

Lancaster University’s School of Mathematical Sciences invites applications for fully funded PhD positions in Pure Mathematics and Statistics.

These positions provide opportunities for candidates to undertake advanced doctoral research under the supervision of experienced academics.

Research Opportunities

Applicants may pursue research projects that align with the interests of academic members of staff.

Potential projects can be developed around the School’s wider research strengths in Pure Mathematics and Statistics.

Applicants are encouraged to:

  • Explore Lancaster University’s research areas
  • Review the academic profiles of potential supervisors
  • Identify research topics that match their academic interests
  • Contact prospective supervisors
  • Discuss possible PhD projects before applying

Some potential research topics and supervisors are available through the School’s Statistics PhD project listings.

Eligibility Requirements for Pure Mathematics and Statistics PhD Studentships

Applicants are generally expected to have a strong academic background in a relevant subject.

The minimum academic requirement is normally:

  • An upper-second class honours degree, equivalent to a UK 2:1, in Mathematics, Statistics or a related discipline

Preference may be given to applicants with advanced qualifications such as:

  • A first-class MSci degree
  • A first-class MMath degree
  • An MSc in Statistics
  • An MSc in Data Science
  • Other relevant postgraduate qualifications

However, exceptional applicants with a strong BSc degree may also be considered.

A competitive PhD application should demonstrate strong academic performance and clear potential for independent research.

Funding Duration for Pure Mathematics and Statistics Students

The funding duration depends on the applicant’s fee status.

According to the available information:

  • UK and EU candidates may receive funding for up to 3.5 years
  • International candidates may receive funding for up to 3 years

The studentship normally includes tuition fees at the applicable funding level and a stipend to support living expenses.

Applicants should confirm the exact financial package and fee arrangements before accepting an offer.

PhD Studentships in Applied Mathematics and Mathematical AI

Lancaster University also offers fully funded PhD opportunities through its Mathematics for AI in Real-world Systems programme.

The programme supports doctoral research connecting mathematical sciences with artificial intelligence and real-world applications.

For the October 2026 entry cycle described in the information provided, these studentships were specifically available to applicants with UK fee status.

Academic Requirements

Applicants were expected to have or be on track to obtain either:

  • A first-class undergraduate degree, or
  • A 2:1 undergraduate degree combined with a merit at master’s level

The degree should be in a subject containing substantial mathematical content.

Relevant disciplines include:

  • Mathematics
  • Statistics
  • Physics
  • Computer Science
  • Engineering
  • Other mathematically intensive subjects

Funding Package

The Mathematics for AI in Real-world Systems PhD programme offers comprehensive funding.

For the October 2026 entry described, the four-year funding package included:

  • Tuition fees
  • An enhanced tax-free living stipend
  • A research, training and support grant

The stipend was listed at approximately £24,403 for 2026, with an increase to approximately £26,388 in the final year.

This enhanced funding package provides significant support for doctoral students undertaking intensive research in mathematical sciences and artificial intelligence.

Application Documents for Mathematical AI Studentships

Applicants were required to contact and discuss their intended project with the prospective lead supervisor before applying.

The application package included:

  1. A current CV of no more than two A4 pages in PDF format
  2. A covering letter of no more than two A4 pages
  3. Academic transcripts
  4. Degree certificates
  5. Confirmation of UK fee status
  6. Information on where the applicant learned about the opportunity

The covering letter was expected to explain:

  • The project the applicant intended to pursue
  • Confirmation that the applicant had discussed the project with the lead supervisor
  • Motivation for pursuing a PhD with the Mathematics for AI in Real-world Systems programme

Applicants were advised to submit complete applications because incomplete applications would not be considered.

Probabilistic Approaches to Artificial Intelligence PhD Opportunities

Lancaster University is also involved in the Probabilistic AI Hub, a major research initiative focused on advancing mathematically rigorous and uncertainty-aware artificial intelligence.

The initiative is supported through a major EPSRC-funded research programme and brings together researchers from multiple leading UK universities.

Participating institutions include:

  • Lancaster University
  • University of Bristol
  • University of Cambridge
  • University of Edinburgh
  • University of Manchester
  • University of Warwick

The initiative also works with industrial partners.

Research Vision of the Probabilistic AI Hub

The Probabilistic AI Hub aims to develop advanced approaches to artificial intelligence based on probability, mathematics and statistics.

The programme seeks to contribute to the development of:

  • Mathematically rigorous AI
  • Scalable AI algorithms
  • Uncertainty-aware machine learning systems
  • Probabilistic reasoning methods
  • Advanced computational algorithms
  • Cross-disciplinary mathematical research

The initiative brings together expertise from:

  • Applied Mathematics
  • Computer Science
  • Probability
  • Statistics
  • Machine Learning

This makes it particularly relevant for researchers interested in the mathematical foundations of modern artificial intelligence.

Research Areas in Probabilistic Artificial Intelligence

Indicative research themes include several emerging areas at the intersection of mathematics and AI.

AI-Scale Probabilistic Reasoning

Possible research topics include:

  • Scalable Monte Carlo methods
  • Conditional sampling
  • Diffusion-generative models
  • Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods
  • AI-assisted computational algorithms

These areas focus on developing computational methods capable of handling increasingly complex AI and data-driven systems.

Mathematical Foundations of Generative Models

Researchers may explore topics involving:

  • Generative modelling
  • Statistical methods
  • Tempering
  • Conditional simulation
  • Diffusion processes
  • Sequential Monte Carlo algorithms
  • New data types and applications

This research area focuses on improving the theoretical understanding of modern generative AI systems.

Structure-Constrained and Informed AI

Another important research direction involves incorporating known information into artificial intelligence models.

For example, researchers may investigate how AI systems can integrate:

  • Physical laws
  • Mathematical constraints
  • Scientific knowledge
  • Structural information

This approach is particularly important for developing AI systems that are more reliable, interpretable and suitable for scientific applications.

Funding for Probabilistic AI PhD Researchers

Successful PhD researchers in the Probabilistic AI programme may receive significant financial support.

The available funding package includes:

  • A tax-free studentship stipend of £20,780 per year
  • Payment of tuition fees
  • Funding for up to 3.5 years, subject to satisfactory progress
  • A training budget
  • Support for attending international conferences

These opportunities provide not only financial support but also opportunities for professional development and international academic engagement.

However, due to tuition fee restrictions, the positions described are available only to applicants eligible for UK fee status.

Student Research Environment at Lancaster University

Lancaster University’s PhD programmes are designed to support students as they transition from taught education into independent research.

For many students, doctoral study represents their first major experience conducting long-term independent academic research.

The School therefore provides an environment intended to help students develop both specialist knowledge and transferable research skills.

PhD students benefit from:

  • Regular academic supervision
  • Guidance from experienced researchers
  • Opportunities to participate in research activities
  • Student seminars
  • Shared research spaces
  • Peer support networks
  • Social activities
  • University-wide academic engagement

Students are encouraged to gradually develop into independent researchers capable of contributing original knowledge to their field.

The skills developed during doctoral study can support careers in:

  • Universities
  • Research institutions
  • Artificial intelligence
  • Data science
  • Technology companies
  • Government research
  • Healthcare
  • Finance
  • Scientific computing
  • Industry

Importance of Choosing the Right PhD Supervisor

Lancaster University emphasises that the research project and supervisor are among the most important considerations when applying for a PhD.

Applicants are therefore encouraged to identify potential supervisors whose research interests align with their own academic goals.

Before applying, candidates should:

  1. Explore the School’s research areas.
  2. Review academic staff profiles.
  3. Identify supervisors working in relevant areas.
  4. Contact potential supervisors.
  5. Discuss possible research projects.
  6. Mention the prospective supervisor in the personal statement where appropriate.

Although applicants may propose their own research ideas, many PhD projects are developed collaboratively with academics.

The final project may therefore take into account:

  • The applicant’s academic background
  • Previous research experience
  • Technical knowledge
  • Research interests
  • The expertise of the prospective supervisor
  • Available funding opportunities

This makes early communication with a potential supervisor an important part of preparing a competitive application.

Examples of Potential PhD Research Topics

Lancaster University has academics supervising research across an exceptionally broad range of mathematical and statistical disciplines.

Potential research themes include:

Mathematics and Theoretical Research

  • Dynamical systems
  • Bifurcation theory
  • Random matrices
  • Optimal transportation
  • Functional analysis
  • Operator algebras
  • Quantum information theory
  • Graph theory
  • Algebraic geometry
  • Representation theory
  • Number theory
  • Combinatorics
  • Discrete probability

Statistics and Probability

  • Bayesian inference
  • MCMC algorithms
  • Particle methods
  • Time series analysis
  • Extreme value analysis
  • Environmental statistics
  • Spatio-temporal modelling
  • Changepoint detection
  • Anomaly detection
  • Statistical ecology

Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning

  • Probabilistic machine learning
  • Optimisation algorithms
  • Generative models
  • AI-scale probabilistic reasoning
  • Machine learning theory
  • Statistical learning
  • Computational Bayesian methods

Applied and Interdisciplinary Mathematics

  • Mathematical biology
  • Epidemiological modelling
  • Medical statistics
  • Computational genomics
  • Climate and environmental modelling
  • Robotics
  • Materials science
  • Mathematical physics
  • Biological networks

This diversity allows prospective students to identify projects aligned with both theoretical interests and practical applications.

How to Apply for a PhD at Lancaster University

The application process generally involves several important stages.

Step 1: Identify Your Research Interests

Before applying, candidates should identify the mathematical, statistical or computational area they want to study.

Applicants should consider questions such as:

  • What subjects am I most interested in?
  • What previous academic experience do I have?
  • Do I prefer theoretical or applied research?
  • Which research topics align with my long-term career goals?
  • Which Lancaster academics work in my area of interest?

Step 2: Identify a Prospective Supervisor

Candidates should review the profiles of academic staff and identify researchers whose expertise aligns with their interests.

Applicants are strongly encouraged to contact potential supervisors to discuss possible research opportunities.

Step 3: Contact the Supervisor

When contacting a prospective supervisor, applicants should clearly introduce themselves and explain:

  • Their academic background
  • Their research interests
  • Relevant projects or research experience
  • Why they are interested in the supervisor’s work
  • Their proposed area of doctoral research

Applicants may also include a CV and academic transcript where appropriate.

Step 4: Complete the Online Application

Applicants must complete the postgraduate application through Lancaster University’s online admissions system.

After creating an account, applicants can enter their personal and academic information and upload supporting documents.

Step 5: Submit Supporting Documents

The standard postgraduate application may require:

  • A completed postgraduate application form
  • Two references
  • Academic transcripts
  • A detailed CV
  • A personal statement
  • English language proficiency evidence where required

Current Lancaster University students or recent graduates may have different reference requirements.

Documents Required for the Application

Applicants should prepare their documents carefully before beginning the online application.

Academic References

Applicants generally need two references.

At least one referee should normally be an academic who can comment on the applicant’s:

  • Academic performance
  • Research potential
  • Analytical abilities
  • Suitability for independent research

Academic Transcripts

Applicants must provide transcripts from previous higher education studies.

Applicants whose documents are not in English may need to provide certified English translations.

Curriculum Vitae

The CV should normally summarise:

  • Academic qualifications
  • Research experience
  • Previous projects
  • Technical skills
  • Relevant employment history
  • Publications, where applicable
  • Academic achievements

For the general application, a detailed CV of up to three pages may be requested.

Personal Statement

The personal statement is an important component of the application.

Applicants should explain:

  • Their research interests
  • Relevant academic experiences
  • Previous research work
  • Technical knowledge
  • The subject area they wish to study
  • Their future academic or professional goals
  • Potential supervisors, where possible

The statement should demonstrate a clear connection between the applicant’s previous background and the proposed doctoral research.

English Language Requirements

Applicants whose first language is not English may be required to demonstrate English language proficiency.

Lancaster University recommends IELTS among the accepted English language tests.

The stated requirement includes:

  • Overall IELTS score of at least 6.5
  • No individual component below 6.0

Applicants with scores below the standard requirement but with individual components of at least 5.5 may potentially be considered for pre-sessional English language programmes.

Applicants should check the latest official language requirements before submitting their application.

Do Applicants Need to Submit a Research Proposal?

The School of Mathematical Sciences does not generally require applicants to submit a formal research proposal.

A research proposal is optional.

However, applicants may benefit from developing a clear understanding of their intended research direction before contacting potential supervisors.

Candidates who require guidance can contact the relevant PhD admissions tutor and indicate their intended programme, such as:

  • PhD Mathematics
  • PhD Statistics
  • PhD Applied Mathematics
  • PhD Mathematical AI

In many cases, the eventual research project is developed in consultation with the prospective supervisor.

Application Interview Process

After the initial screening process, applicants being considered for admission may be invited to an online interview.

The interview is typically conducted by a small academic panel.

The process generally involves:

  1. Submission of the application
  2. Initial screening
  3. Invitation to an online interview for shortlisted applicants
  4. Academic assessment by the relevant committee
  5. Decision regarding admission
  6. Consideration for available studentship funding where applicable

The Postgraduate Research Committee makes decisions regarding offers and competitive departmental funding.

Applicants should be prepared to discuss:

  • Their academic background
  • Previous research experience
  • Mathematical or statistical knowledge
  • Research interests
  • Motivation for pursuing a PhD
  • Understanding of the proposed research area
  • Long-term career ambitions

Deadline for Lancaster University PhD Studentships

The School of Mathematical Sciences has a general studentship deadline of 31 January.

Applications received by this deadline receive equal consideration for available studentships.

Applications submitted after the deadline may still be considered if funding remains available.

Final studentship decisions are normally made by April.

However, applicants should note that specific programmes and funding routes may have different deadlines.

For example, the Applied Mathematics and Mathematical AI studentships for the October 2026 intake listed a deadline of 17:00 GMT on 31 January 2026.

Prospective applicants should always confirm the latest deadline directly through the official Lancaster University website, particularly when applying for future entry cycles.

When Should You Apply?

Lancaster University recommends preparing PhD applications well in advance.

Applications for October entry in the following academic year are normally considered between October and May.

To improve the chances of securing both admission and funding, prospective applicants should ideally:

  • Begin researching programmes 6–12 months in advance
  • Identify potential supervisors early
  • Contact supervisors before the funding deadline
  • Prepare academic documents early
  • Request references in advance
  • Complete English language requirements where necessary
  • Submit the application before competitive funding deadlines

Many funding opportunities for October entry close before March of the same year.

Early preparation is therefore particularly important for applicants seeking fully funded positions.

Tips for Submitting a Strong PhD Application

Competition for funded PhD positions can be significant. Applicants should therefore approach the process strategically.

1. Contact Potential Supervisors Early

Do not wait until the final deadline to begin discussions with academics.

Early communication can help applicants:

  • Understand potential projects
  • Determine whether their background is suitable
  • Receive guidance on research directions
  • Develop a stronger application

2. Demonstrate Strong Academic Preparation

A competitive application should demonstrate knowledge relevant to the intended research area.

Applicants should highlight:

  • Strong grades
  • Relevant coursework
  • Research projects
  • Dissertation work
  • Programming skills
  • Mathematical modelling experience
  • Statistical analysis experience

3. Tailor the Personal Statement

Avoid submitting a generic statement.

Explain clearly:

  • Why you want to pursue doctoral research
  • Why you selected Lancaster University
  • Why the particular research area interests you
  • How your previous background prepares you for the programme

4. Choose Referees Carefully

Academic referees should ideally know the applicant’s work well enough to comment on research potential.

Strong references can provide evidence of:

  • Intellectual ability
  • Research independence
  • Technical competence
  • Academic motivation

5. Apply Before the Funding Deadline

Submitting an application early can increase opportunities to be considered for competitive funding.

Do not assume that funding will remain available after the main deadline.

APPLY HERE

Benefits of Pursuing a PhD at Lancaster University

A PhD at Lancaster University’s School of Mathematical Sciences offers more than an advanced academic qualification.

Students have opportunities to develop expertise and transferable skills relevant to multiple sectors.

Potential benefits include:

  • Advanced specialist knowledge
  • Independent research experience
  • Access to experienced academic supervisors
  • Interdisciplinary collaboration
  • Training in advanced research methodologies
  • Opportunities to participate in academic seminars
  • Peer learning and research networks
  • Conference participation opportunities
  • International research exposure
  • Career preparation for academia and industry

For students interested in emerging technologies, the School’s work in artificial intelligence, probabilistic machine learning and computational methods also provides opportunities to engage with rapidly developing research fields.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Lancaster University Fully Funded PhD Studentships.

Conclusion

The Lancaster University School of Mathematical Sciences PhD opportunities provide an important pathway for talented graduates seeking advanced research training in Mathematics, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Artificial Intelligence and related disciplines.

With research areas ranging from Pure Mathematics and probability to machine learning, mathematical modelling, statistical science and probabilistic AI, the School offers a broad academic environment for students with diverse research interests.

Several funding routes are available, including Research Council studentships, departmental funding, industry-supported projects and specialist doctoral training programmes. Depending on the specific studentship, successful applicants may receive tuition fee support, tax-free living stipends, research training funding and opportunities to participate in international academic activities.

Applicants are strongly encouraged to begin preparing early, identify potential supervisors whose expertise matches their interests and submit complete applications before relevant funding deadlines. Since PhD projects and funding opportunities vary, prospective students should carefully review the latest information on Lancaster University’s official postgraduate research pages before applying.

For ambitious graduates seeking to contribute to mathematical research, artificial intelligence, statistics and other quantitative disciplines, Lancaster University presents a valuable opportunity to develop advanced research skills while working within a highly active and internationally connected academic environment.

item.content:encoded:
The NTU AI-for-X Postdoctoral Fellowship 2026 is a prestigious postdoctoral research opportunity in Singapore designed for outstanding early-career researchers seeking to apply Artificial Intelligence (AI) to scientific discovery and advance research across science, technology, engineering, mathematics and medicine.

Jointly supported by Nanyang Technological University (NTU) and Singapore’s National Research Foundation (NRF), the AI-for-X Postdoctoral Fellowship (AI4X-PDF) seeks to attract promising researchers who can use AI to address important scientific problems and contribute to the development of Singapore’s AI-for-Science ecosystem.

The programme is particularly relevant to researchers working at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence and STEM disciplines, offering a combination of research funding, competitive remuneration, access to advanced computing and research infrastructure, mentorship, AI training and academic career development.

For researchers who have recently completed a PhD and are looking to establish an independent research profile, the fellowship provides an opportunity to develop ambitious research while working within one of Singapore’s leading research universities.

Opportunity Overview

  • Opportunity: NTU AI-for-X Postdoctoral Fellowship (AI4X-PDF) 2026
  • Host institution: Nanyang Technological University (NTU)
  • Location: Singapore
  • Opportunity type: Postdoctoral Fellowship
  • Research focus: Artificial Intelligence applied to Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics and Medicine
  • Funding duration: Up to 4 years
  • Research grant: SGD 250,000
  • PhD requirement: PhD or equivalent in a STEM field, conferred in 2023 or later
  • Mentorship: Project Mentor and AI Mentor
  • Expected commencement: By 31 March 2027
  • Application deadline: 30 October 2026 at 23:59 Singapore Time (UTC/GMT+8)
  • Application method: Online application through NTU’s application portal

About the NTU AI-for-X Postdoctoral Fellowship

The NTU AI-for-X Postdoctoral Fellowship is designed around the idea of using Artificial Intelligence as a powerful tool for scientific research and discovery.

Rather than focusing exclusively on conventional AI research, the fellowship encourages researchers to explore how AI can be integrated into other scientific and technological disciplines to address complex research questions.

The programme therefore targets researchers who can demonstrate both strong scientific expertise and a clear vision for applying AI to meaningful scientific challenges.

The fellowship forms part of NTU’s broader research ecosystem and is jointly supported by NTU and Singapore’s National Research Foundation. Successful fellows will be co-funded through the NRF Postdoctoral Award (NRF-PA) framework.

Through this model, fellows can develop research at the intersection of AI and STEM while gaining access to an environment intended to nurture future research leaders.

Why the NTU AI-for-X Fellowship Is a Significant Opportunity

Artificial Intelligence is increasingly being used to accelerate scientific discovery, analyse complex datasets, develop predictive models, improve experimentation and address problems that would otherwise require significant amounts of time and resources.

The AI4X-PDF responds to this growing role of AI in scientific research by supporting researchers who can combine disciplinary expertise with AI-driven approaches.

The fellowship can therefore be particularly valuable for researchers who want to:

  • Develop an independent research programme.
  • Apply AI techniques to scientific problems.
  • Build a strong international research profile.
  • Work alongside researchers across different STEM disciplines.
  • Access advanced AI platforms and computing infrastructure.
  • Receive structured mentorship from experienced researchers.
  • Strengthen their academic career prospects.
  • Develop research that could contribute to future scientific breakthroughs.
  • Prepare for future tenure-track or equivalent academic positions.

The programme is positioned not simply as a short-term postdoctoral appointment but as a platform for developing researchers into future scientific and academic leaders.

Key Benefits of the NTU AI-for-X Postdoctoral Fellowship

1. Up to Four Years of Funding

One of the major attractions of the fellowship is its potential duration. Selected researchers can receive up to four years of funding, providing a substantial period in which to develop and advance an ambitious research programme.

A longer fellowship period can allow researchers to move beyond preliminary investigations and develop deeper research programmes, publications, collaborations and scientific outputs.

2. Competitive Remuneration and Benefits

Successful fellows will receive competitive remuneration and benefits as part of the fellowship package.

This provides financial support while researchers concentrate on their research and professional development at NTU.

3. SGD 250,000 Research Grant

The fellowship includes a substantial SGD 250,000 research grant.

This research funding can provide an important foundation for developing a research programme, supporting the resources and activities required to investigate the proposed scientific problem.

For early-career researchers seeking to establish a distinctive research profile, access to dedicated research funding can also strengthen their ability to pursue ambitious projects.

4. Continued Funding During a Transition to a Tenure-Track Role

The programme also provides continued funding if a fellow transitions to a tenure-track or equivalent position during the award period, subject to the programme’s conditions.

This feature can make the fellowship particularly attractive to researchers who have long-term academic ambitions.

Rather than treating the postdoctoral period as an isolated stage of a research career, the programme provides a pathway toward broader academic development.

5. Access to NTU AI Platforms and Research Facilities

Fellows will have access to NTU’s AI platforms, research facilities and computing resources.

This is particularly important for researchers whose projects require significant computational capacity, AI infrastructure or access to specialised research facilities.

The availability of institutional infrastructure can enable researchers to test, develop and scale AI-driven approaches to scientific questions.

6. AI Training and Mentorship

Selected fellows will benefit from structured AI training and mentorship involving NTU faculty working across AI and STEM disciplines.

This interdisciplinary approach can be valuable for researchers whose primary expertise lies in a scientific field but who want to strengthen their ability to integrate AI into their research.

7. Teaching and Academic Career Development

The fellowship also includes coaching in university-level teaching.

Teaching development can be particularly useful for researchers preparing for academic careers because successful academics are often expected to demonstrate both research and teaching capabilities.

The teaching component therefore supports the broader transition toward an academic career.

Who Can Apply for the NTU AI-for-X Postdoctoral Fellowship?

The fellowship is aimed at early-career researchers who have recently completed a PhD or equivalent qualification in a STEM field.

Applicants must meet several eligibility requirements, including the following:

PhD Qualification

Applicants must hold a PhD or equivalent qualification in a STEM field.

According to the fellowship information, the PhD must have been conferred in 2023 or later.

This means the opportunity is primarily targeted at researchers who are relatively early in their postdoctoral careers rather than established senior researchers.

STEM Background

The applicant’s doctoral background must be in a STEM field.

The fellowship information specifically frames its research scope broadly across:

  • Science
  • Technology
  • Engineering
  • Mathematics
  • Medicine

Applicants should therefore consider whether their disciplinary background and proposed research fit within the fellowship’s STEM and AI-for-Science focus.

Strong Academic and Research Record

Candidates are expected to demonstrate a strong academic and research record.

This is a competitive postdoctoral fellowship, so applicants should be prepared to demonstrate evidence of research excellence through their academic achievements, publications and broader research contributions.

AI-Integrated Research Proposal

A central requirement is a compelling research proposal that clearly integrates Artificial Intelligence to solve a scientific problem.

This is one of the most important aspects of the application.

Applicants should not simply propose a conventional scientific research project and mention AI as an additional component. The proposal should clearly explain how AI contributes to addressing the underlying scientific challenge.

A strong proposal should therefore establish a logical connection between:

  1. The scientific problem.
  2. The limitations of existing approaches.
  3. The proposed AI-based approach.
  4. The scientific value of applying AI.
  5. The expected research outcomes.

NTU Project Mentor

Applicants must identify an NTU faculty member as a Project Mentor.

The mentor will provide disciplinary guidance and support the proposed research within the NTU research environment.

Applicants should therefore carefully consider potential faculty mentors whose expertise aligns with their proposed research.

Mentorship Structure

Each selected fellow will be paired with two important forms of mentorship.

Project Mentor

The Project Mentor will support the fellow in their research field and provide disciplinary guidance related to the proposed scientific project.

AI Mentor

The fellow will also receive an AI Mentor, who will be assigned or selected after the award.

The AI Mentor is intended to support the integration of Artificial Intelligence into the fellow’s scientific research.

This dual-mentor model reflects the central purpose of the fellowship: bringing together domain-specific scientific expertise and AI capabilities.

Application Process for the NTU AI-for-X Postdoctoral Fellowship 2026

Applications must be submitted electronically through the official NTU Online Application Portal.

Applicants should prepare their documents carefully before submitting the application because the fellowship requires several supporting materials.

Required Application Documents

Applicants are required to submit the following:

1. Cover Letter

A cover letter should accompany the application and provide a clear overview of the applicant’s background, research interests and motivation for applying.

It should complement rather than simply repeat information contained in the CV.

2. Comprehensive CV

Applicants must provide a comprehensive CV.

The CV should include the applicant’s Scopus Author ID and a full publication list.

Researchers should ensure that their academic achievements, publications, research experience and other relevant accomplishments are presented clearly.

3. Official PhD Transcript or Degree Certificate

Applicants must provide an official transcript or degree certificate in English for their PhD.

The documentation should demonstrate the required doctoral qualification.

4. Research Proposal

Applicants must submit a research proposal of no more than two pages.

The proposal is particularly important because the fellowship is focused on applying AI to scientific problems.

The proposal should clearly demonstrate:

  • The scientific problem being addressed.
  • Why the problem is important.
  • The proposed research approach.
  • How Artificial Intelligence will be integrated.
  • The expected scientific contribution.
  • Why the proposed research is suitable for the NTU environment.

Applicants should also follow the official proposal template provided by NTU.

5. Contact Information for Two Referees

Applicants must provide contact information for two referees.

One of the referees must be the applicant’s PhD Supervisor.

Applicants should contact their referees before submitting the application and confirm that they are willing to provide recommendation reports.

NTU will contact the referees after the application has been submitted.

6. Top Three Publications

Applicants are required to submit their top three publications in PDF format.

Applicants should therefore carefully select the publications that best demonstrate their research quality, expertise and potential.

The strongest publications will generally be those most closely connected to the applicant’s research trajectory and proposed AI-for-science project.

7. Mentor’s Support Letter

Applicants must also submit a support letter from their NTU mentor.

The mentor’s support letter should be attached to the research proposal and uploaded as one combined file in the research proposal section of the application.

This makes early engagement with a prospective NTU faculty mentor particularly important.

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the NTU AI-for-X Postdoctoral Fellowship 2026 is:

30 October 2026 at 23:59 Singapore Time (UTC/GMT+8).

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day to submit their applications, particularly because obtaining mentor support, preparing a two-page research proposal and securing referee agreement can require considerable advance preparation.

APPLY HERE

Fellowship Commencement Requirement

Successful applicants must be available to commence the fellowship by 31 March 2027.

Applicants should therefore consider their current employment, research commitments, visa arrangements and other obligations when assessing their ability to take up the fellowship within the required timeframe.

Online Briefing Sessions

NTU is offering online briefing sessions for prospective applicants.

The sessions are intended to help researchers understand the fellowship and the application process before submitting their applications.

The briefings cover areas including:

  • Fellowship objectives.
  • Research opportunities.
  • Eligibility requirements.
  • Funding and benefits.
  • Application procedures.
  • Selection timeline.
  • Questions from prospective applicants.

Four sessions are scheduled in Singapore Time:

Date Time Registration
Tuesday, 1 September 2026 10:00–11:00 AM Registration required
Wednesday, 2 September 2026 2:00–3:00 PM Registration required
Thursday, 1 October 2026 10:00–11:00 AM Registration required
Friday, 2 October 2026 2:00–3:00 PM Registration required

Applicants can register for and attend any one of the available sessions.

Registration is required, and the Microsoft Teams meeting link is provided in the registration confirmation after successful registration.

Because the first two sessions take place in September, prospective applicants who have not yet attended a briefing may wish to consider one of the October sessions.

How to Prepare a Competitive Application

The competitive nature of the AI4X-PDF means applicants should approach the application strategically.

1. Develop a Clearly Defined Scientific Problem

The research proposal should begin with a scientifically meaningful problem.

Applicants should demonstrate that the proposed problem is important and that addressing it could produce meaningful scientific or technological value.

2. Explain Why AI Is Necessary

The application should clearly establish why AI is appropriate for the proposed problem.

Rather than simply stating that AI will be used, applicants should explain what AI enables them to accomplish that conventional approaches may not achieve as effectively.

3. Demonstrate Interdisciplinary Potential

Since the fellowship sits at the intersection of AI and STEM, applicants should demonstrate their ability to connect their disciplinary expertise with AI methodologies.

The strongest applications are likely to show a genuine integration rather than treating AI as an unrelated add-on.

4. Identify an Appropriate NTU Mentor

Finding a suitable NTU faculty Project Mentor is a critical part of the application.

Applicants should research NTU faculty members and identify researchers whose expertise, facilities and research interests align with the proposed project.

A strong mentor-project match can help demonstrate that the proposed research can realistically be implemented within the NTU research environment.

5. Select Publications Strategically

Applicants should use the three-publication requirement to showcase their strongest research.

The selected publications should help establish the applicant’s expertise and demonstrate their potential to conduct high-quality independent research.

6. Make the Two-Page Proposal Focused

Because the proposal is limited to two pages, applicants need to communicate their research vision efficiently.

Every section should contribute to answering the central question: What important scientific problem will be solved, and how will AI enable the research?

7. Engage Referees Early

Since two referees are required and one must be the PhD Supervisor, applicants should approach referees well before the deadline.

Referees should agree to provide reports before the application is submitted.

8. Follow the Document Requirements Carefully

Applicants should check file formats, document completeness and submission requirements before submitting.

Particular attention should be paid to the requirement that the mentor’s support letter be combined with the research proposal and uploaded as a single file in the appropriate application section.

Who Is Eligible by Country, Race and Continent?

The information provided for the NTU AI-for-X Postdoctoral Fellowship does not state a specific nationality, race or country restriction.

Therefore, the published eligibility criteria do not identify the fellowship as being restricted to applicants from a particular African, Asian, European, American or other regional group.

In practical terms, the opportunity is presented as an international research fellowship for eligible early-career researchers, with eligibility primarily determined by academic and research requirements rather than race or geographic origin.

Applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Oceania and other regions may therefore consider applying if they satisfy the fellowship’s stated requirements. However, applicants should rely on NTU’s official eligibility rules for the final determination of their individual eligibility.

The key requirements remain the possession of a qualifying STEM PhD conferred in 2023 or later, a strong academic and research record, an AI-integrated scientific research proposal, an NTU faculty Project Mentor and availability to commence by 31 March 2027.

Visit HERE for more information about the NTU AI-for-X Postdoctoral Fellowship 2026.

Category of People Who Qualify

The opportunity is primarily suitable for:

  • Early-career researchers.
  • Recent PhD graduates.
  • Researchers with a PhD or equivalent in a STEM field.
  • Researchers whose doctoral qualification was conferred in 2023 or later.
  • Scientists interested in applying AI to scientific discovery.
  • Technology and engineering researchers working on AI-enabled scientific problems.
  • Mathematics researchers developing AI-related scientific applications.
  • Medical researchers with suitable AI-for-science research proposals.
  • Researchers with a strong academic and research record.
  • Applicants capable of developing a compelling AI-integrated research proposal.
  • Researchers able to identify an NTU faculty member willing to serve as Project Mentor.
  • Researchers intending to pursue an academic or research leadership career.

Conclusion

The NTU AI-for-X Postdoctoral Fellowship 2026 represents a major opportunity for early-career STEM researchers who want to build research careers at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence and scientific discovery.

With up to four years of funding, a SGD 250,000 research grant, competitive remuneration, access to AI platforms and research facilities, structured AI training, interdisciplinary mentorship and teaching-development support, the fellowship provides researchers with resources to develop ambitious research programmes and strengthen their academic trajectories.

Its emphasis on using AI to solve scientific problems makes it particularly relevant to researchers who can demonstrate a clear connection between their disciplinary expertise and emerging AI methodologies. The requirement for an NTU Project Mentor also means that applicants should begin identifying suitable faculty collaborators well before submitting their applications.

Eligible researchers should pay particular attention to the PhD completion requirement of 2023 or later, the need for a strong academic and research record, the two-page AI-integrated research proposal, the three selected publications, referee requirements and mentor support letter.

The application deadline is 30 October 2026 at 23:59 Singapore Time (UTC/GMT+8), while successful fellows must be able to commence the fellowship by 31 March 2027.

For researchers seeking to contribute to the rapidly developing field of AI-for-Science while building an internationally competitive academic research career, the NTU AI-for-X Postdoctoral Fellowship offers an opportunity to combine scientific expertise, Artificial Intelligence, interdisciplinary collaboration and substantial research support within Singapore’s research ecosystem.

For more global Fellowship opportunities, visit OFY HERE.

item.content:encoded:
NASA is offering an exciting opportunity for students interested in communications, journalism, multimedia production, public engagement, digital media, photography, marketing, graphic design, and science communication to gain hands-on professional experience through its Multimedia, Social Media, Public Engagement, and Internal Communications Internship.

Hosted at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) in Greenbelt, Maryland, the internship provides students with the opportunity to work alongside experienced writers, multimedia producers, public affairs professionals, and experience designers. Successful interns will contribute to communications activities connected to some of NASA’s most significant scientific missions and discoveries.

The opportunity is designed for students who are passionate about storytelling and interested in translating complex scientific information into engaging content for diverse audiences. Interns may work on content and campaigns related to NASA missions such as the Hubble Space Telescope, James Webb Space Telescope, Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, Artemis lunar exploration, Earth observation satellites, and solar science missions.

The application deadline is September 14, 2026.

About the NASA Communications Internship

NASA internships provide educational, hands-on experiences that allow students to explore research, operations, technology, communications, and other professional fields connected to the agency’s work.

This particular internship focuses on science communication and public engagement. NASA is seeking students who can help communicate scientific discoveries, space exploration activities, technological developments, and educational initiatives to the public through compelling stories and creative media.

Students will become part of a dynamic communications environment where storytelling intersects with science, technology, creativity, and public engagement.

The internship offers exposure to numerous areas of professional communication, including:

  • Journalism
  • Science writing
  • Multimedia production
  • Social media communication
  • Public relations
  • Media relations
  • Strategic communications
  • Digital communications
  • Marketing
  • Graphic design
  • Photography
  • Videography
  • Broadcast journalism
  • Event planning
  • Public engagement
  • Internal communications
  • Digital storytelling
  • Livestream production
  • Web content development

The internship is particularly suitable for students who want to build careers in science communication, journalism, public affairs, digital media, creative production, or strategic communications.

Gain Experience Communicating NASA’s Scientific Discoveries

One of the most exciting aspects of the internship is the opportunity to contribute to communications surrounding major NASA science missions.

NASA’s communications teams are responsible for helping the public understand scientific discoveries and exploration activities. Interns may gain exposure to projects involving some of the world’s most recognized space science programs.

These may include stories and communications related to:

Hubble Space Telescope

The Hubble Space Telescope has transformed humanity’s understanding of the universe through decades of observations and discoveries. Communications professionals help translate complex astronomical research into stories that can be understood and appreciated by global audiences.

James Webb Space Telescope

The James Webb Space Telescope is one of NASA’s most significant scientific observatories. Its discoveries generate enormous public interest, requiring skilled communicators who can explain groundbreaking research through articles, videos, graphics, social media, and other forms of media.

Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope

Students may also gain exposure to communications related to NASA’s Roman Space Telescope and its mission to explore fundamental questions about the universe.

Artemis Program

NASA’s Artemis missions represent a new era of lunar exploration. Communications surrounding Artemis involve public engagement, multimedia storytelling, digital campaigns, educational outreach, and media relations.

Earth Science and Remote Sensing

NASA’s Earth-observing satellites provide critical information about our changing planet. Communicators play an important role in sharing scientific findings about climate, weather, environmental change, ecosystems, and other Earth science topics.

Solar Science

NASA also studies the Sun and regularly communicates discoveries from solar missions. Students interested in translating complex scientific concepts into engaging stories may find this area particularly rewarding.

Two Major Internship Focus Areas

The NASA internship posting covers two major professional focus areas. Applicants can indicate their preference for one area or express interest in a combination of both.

1. Multimedia Newsroom

Students selected for Multimedia Newsroom roles will have opportunities to work on complex communications campaigns and multimedia storytelling initiatives.

Potential activities may include creating:

  • Web features
  • News stories
  • Articles
  • Videos
  • Social media content
  • Digital campaigns
  • Media interview materials
  • Livestream productions
  • Multimedia presentations
  • Digital storytelling projects

The Multimedia Newsroom pathway provides flexibility for students to focus on areas that match their professional interests and existing skills.

Possible areas of specialization include:

  • Video production
  • Video editing
  • Writing
  • Journalism
  • Digital storytelling
  • Social media
  • Multimedia production
  • Photography
  • Science communication

This pathway may be particularly valuable for students who want practical experience working in a fast-paced communications environment.

2. Public Engagement

The Public Engagement positions focus on connecting NASA’s work with different audiences through outreach activities, campaigns, events, and engagement initiatives.

Interns may contribute to areas such as:

  • Public outreach
  • Communications campaign design
  • Event planning
  • Event coordination
  • Tour organization
  • Internal workforce engagement
  • Photography
  • Graphic design
  • Exhibitions and displays
  • Audience engagement

Students may have opportunities to focus on specific areas depending on their interests and the needs of the communications team.

Potential areas include:

  • Tours and visitor engagement
  • Graphics and visual displays
  • Photography
  • Event planning
  • Workforce engagement
  • Public outreach
  • Internal communications

Applicants can indicate whether they prefer the Multimedia Newsroom, Public Engagement, or a combination of both areas.

What Will NASA Interns Do?

The internship offers broad exposure to communications work. NASA describes the responsibilities using an extensive range of activities that reflect the creative and multidisciplinary nature of the role.

Interns may be involved in activities such as:

  • Writing
  • Designing
  • Researching
  • Creating
  • Editing
  • Hosting
  • Engaging audiences
  • Developing communication materials
  • Analyzing content performance
  • Producing multimedia content
  • Conducting interviews
  • Managing digital content
  • Creating captions
  • Photographing events and activities
  • Shooting videos
  • Monitoring communications platforms
  • Updating information
  • Networking
  • Managing projects
  • Tracking communication activities
  • Building campaigns
  • Exploring creative storytelling approaches

The internship therefore provides an opportunity to experience multiple dimensions of modern communications rather than focusing exclusively on one narrow area.

Build Professional Skills in Science Communication

Students participating in the internship can develop and strengthen skills that are increasingly important across journalism, communications, marketing, media, and digital industries.

The skills highlighted for the opportunity include:

  • Creative writing
  • AP writing style
  • Writing and editing
  • Writing and interviewing
  • Video and photography knowledge
  • Video production
  • Video editing
  • Social media management
  • Photography
  • Digital photography
  • Livestream production
  • Digital media
  • Digital communications
  • Event planning
  • Event coordination
  • Blogging
  • Science education

These skills can be valuable for students pursuing careers in:

  • Journalism
  • Public relations
  • Corporate communications
  • Science communication
  • Digital marketing
  • Social media management
  • Multimedia production
  • Broadcasting
  • Public affairs
  • Photography
  • Videography
  • Strategic communications
  • Content creation
  • Marketing communications
  • Public engagement

Who Should Apply?

NASA is particularly interested in students pursuing academic programs related to communications, media, journalism, marketing, writing, design, and related disciplines.

The internship welcomes students pursuing degrees in areas such as:

  • Journalism
  • Communications
  • Media relations
  • Science writing
  • Convergence journalism
  • Broadcast journalism
  • Public relations
  • Strategic communications
  • Marketing
  • Graphic design
  • Museum design
  • Photography

The preferred academic fields listed for the opportunity also include disciplines connected to:

  • Communication and media studies
  • Journalism and related programs
  • Public relations
  • Advertising
  • Applied communication
  • Publishing
  • Radio
  • Television
  • Digital communication
  • Creative writing
  • Cinematography
  • Film and video production
  • Design and applied arts
  • Audiovisual communications technologies
  • Graphic communications
  • Marketing

However, NASA emphasizes that the strongest candidates are not necessarily limited to traditional communications backgrounds.

Students with scientific knowledge and strong communication skills may find the opportunity especially rewarding. Similarly, talented communicators with a strong interest in science and space exploration are encouraged to consider the internship.

NASA notes that successful candidates often include:

  • Scientists with a talent for communication and storytelling
  • Skilled communicators interested in science
  • Creative students with curiosity about space and scientific discovery
  • Students who enjoy translating complex ideas for broader audiences
  • Individuals interested in combining science and creative communication

Key Attributes NASA Is Looking For

Beyond technical qualifications, NASA is looking for students with particular personal and professional characteristics.

Key attributes include:

Unbounded Curiosity

NASA is looking for individuals who are naturally curious and eager to learn. Interns will be exposed to scientific discoveries, technological developments, and complex concepts that require a genuine interest in exploration.

Creative Spirit

The ability to think creatively is important in science communication. Interns may need to find innovative ways to transform technical information into engaging stories, videos, social media posts, and experiences.

Passion for Storytelling

Effective communication requires more than simply presenting facts. NASA is seeking students who can identify compelling stories and communicate them in ways that connect with diverse audiences.

Interest in Science

Although a science degree is not required for all applicants, students with experience or interest in scientific subjects may find the internship particularly valuable.

Ability to Engage Diverse Audiences

NASA communicates with scientists, students, educators, policymakers, journalists, and members of the general public. Interns should therefore be interested in creating content that can connect with different audiences.

Internship Location

The internship is based at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in:

Greenbelt, Maryland, United States

Goddard Space Flight Center is one of NASA’s major centers and plays an important role in scientific research, space missions, Earth observation, astrophysics, heliophysics, and technology development.

The opportunity is primarily designed as an in-person internship.

While some day-to-day flexibility may be possible, NASA states that much of the work requires interns to be physically present.

Students should therefore be prepared for an on-site professional experience in Greenbelt, Maryland.

Full-Time Work Schedule

The NASA internship is considered a full-time opportunity.

Selected interns should expect to dedicate approximately:

40 hours per week

The normal schedule is expected to take place:

  • Monday through Friday
  • During regular working hours

NASA may make some adjustments for students with mid-day academic classes. However, the organization indicates that students with fewer scheduling conflicts are likely to have the most optimal internship experience.

Applicants should carefully consider their academic schedules and availability before applying.

NASA Internship Session

The internship is scheduled for:

Spring 2027

Students interested in participating should ensure they are available during the Spring 2027 internship period and capable of committing to the full-time schedule.

Application Tips for Prospective Candidates

NASA provides specific guidance for applicants preparing their internship submissions.

Applicants are encouraged to include a strong personal statement explaining their interests and career objectives.

A competitive personal statement should clearly address:

  • Why you are interested in the internship
  • Your professional and academic objectives
  • How the internship fits into your career goals
  • Relevant coursework
  • Previous internships
  • Work experience
  • Communication skills
  • Creative abilities
  • Interest in science or space exploration

Applicants should also consider including links to relevant work samples.

Depending on the applicant’s background, a portfolio may include:

  • Published articles
  • Blog posts
  • Writing samples
  • Photography portfolios
  • Videos
  • Social media campaigns
  • Graphic design projects
  • Multimedia productions
  • Digital communication campaigns
  • Journalism work
  • Interview samples
  • Websites
  • Creative storytelling projects

Providing relevant examples of previous work can help demonstrate practical skills and professional interests.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Students interested in the NASA internship should approach their application strategically.

1. Write a Clear Personal Statement

Explain your academic and professional journey and demonstrate why this particular internship is relevant to your career goals.

Avoid submitting a generic statement. Instead, connect your experiences directly to:

  • Science communication
  • Multimedia storytelling
  • Public engagement
  • NASA’s mission
  • Digital communications
  • Journalism
  • Public outreach

2. Highlight Relevant Coursework

Mention academic courses that demonstrate relevant knowledge.

Examples may include:

  • Journalism
  • Public relations
  • Digital media
  • Photography
  • Video production
  • Graphic design
  • Marketing
  • Science communication
  • Creative writing
  • Broadcasting

3. Demonstrate Practical Experience

Include relevant professional or extracurricular experiences.

This could include:

  • University media projects
  • Student journalism
  • Communication internships
  • Social media management
  • Photography
  • Video production
  • Blogging
  • Event organization
  • Marketing campaigns
  • Science outreach

4. Develop a Strong Portfolio

Where possible, provide links to work that demonstrate your abilities.

Applicants should prioritize quality and relevance over simply submitting a large number of examples.

5. Explain Your Career Goals

NASA wants to understand how the internship fits into your broader professional aspirations.

Clearly explain how the experience would contribute to your future career in areas such as:

  • Science journalism
  • Communications
  • Public affairs
  • Multimedia production
  • Strategic communications
  • Digital storytelling
  • Space communication
  • Public engagement

6. Show Genuine Interest in NASA’s Mission

Applicants should research NASA’s scientific programs and identify areas that genuinely interest them.

Demonstrating familiarity with NASA’s work can help applicants develop a more focused and convincing application.

Eligibility Requirements

According to the opportunity details, applicants must meet the citizenship and academic requirements outlined by NASA.

Citizenship Requirement

Applicants must be:

United States citizens

This opportunity is specifically listed as open to U.S. citizens only.

Academic Level

Eligible students include:

  • Undergraduate freshmen
  • Undergraduate sophomores
  • Undergraduate juniors
  • Undergraduate seniors
  • Graduate Master’s students

Student Status

Applicants must be students pursuing an eligible academic program.

Age Requirement

NASA internship opportunities generally provide educational hands-on experiences for undergraduate and graduate students aged 16 and above.

Applicants should carefully review all requirements and conditions on the official NASA internship platform before submitting their applications.

Important Dates

Students interested in this NASA internship should take note of the following dates:

  • Registration Start Date: June 12, 2026
  • Registration End Date / Application Deadline: September 14, 2026
  • Internship Session: Spring 2027

Applicants are strongly encouraged to submit their applications before the deadline rather than waiting until the final day.

Why Apply for the NASA Communications Internship?

An internship with NASA can provide students with an exceptional opportunity to combine academic learning with practical professional experience.

Key advantages of the opportunity include:

Work with Experienced Professionals

Interns will collaborate with professionals including:

  • Writers
  • Multimedia producers
  • Public affairs officers
  • Communications specialists
  • Experience designers

Gain Practical Portfolio Experience

Students may contribute to real communication activities and develop work that can strengthen future professional portfolios.

Explore Multiple Communication Fields

The broad nature of the internship allows students to gain exposure to writing, multimedia, social media, public engagement, events, photography, and other communication disciplines.

Connect Science and Storytelling

The internship provides a unique opportunity to learn how complex scientific discoveries can be transformed into compelling and accessible stories.

Build Professional Networks

Working within a major scientific organization can provide opportunities to connect with professionals and other students with similar career interests.

Gain Experience in a Globally Recognized Organization

NASA is one of the world’s most recognized scientific and space organizations. Professional experience gained through the internship can be valuable for students pursuing future opportunities in communications, science, technology, media, and public engagement.

How to Apply

Interested and eligible students should apply through the official NASA internship and STEM Gateway platforms.

Applicants should carefully review the opportunity details and prepare all required application materials before submission.

The official NASA internship website provides additional information about NASA internship programs.

Applicants can also explore the NASA STEM Gateway for additional opportunities and information.

APPLY HERE

Application Contact

Visit HERE to learn more about the NASA Multimedia, Social Media, Public Engagement and Internal Communications Internship 2027 for Undergraduate and Graduate Students.

For additional information regarding NASA internships, the engagement contact listed is: nasa-internships@mail.nasa.gov

Conclusion

The NASA Multimedia, Social Media, Public Engagement, and Internal Communications Internship offers a valuable opportunity for aspiring communicators, journalists, content creators, multimedia specialists, photographers, designers, and science storytellers to gain hands-on experience within one of the world’s most influential scientific organizations.

Through the Spring 2027 internship, selected students will have the opportunity to explore the intersection of science, creativity, technology, and public communication. Whether contributing to multimedia storytelling, developing digital content, supporting public engagement campaigns, planning events, producing videos, or helping communicate scientific discoveries, interns can gain broad exposure to the professional communications ecosystem behind NASA’s scientific missions.

Students with a strong curiosity, creative mindset, passion for storytelling, and interest in science should strongly consider this opportunity. A carefully prepared application, compelling personal statement, and relevant portfolio can help applicants demonstrate how their academic background and professional ambitions align with the internship.

With the September 14, 2026 deadline approaching, eligible students should begin preparing their application materials early and ensure they clearly communicate their skills, interests, and career objectives.
